headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: aci’s broad egress plus gpt-engineer’s filesystem/code execution can move sensitive CRM/email data into generated code and external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through Slack, email, Notion, Sheets, and MCP-style function calls, while gpt-engineer reads/writes a project directory and can execute generated code. A shared workspace or copied outputs create a plausible instruction-hijack path, though not a guaranteed one. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or project files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a project directory or message channel, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before pasting aci output into gpt-engineer.
Prefix imported text with clear delimiters and treat it as data only.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Strip tool instructions from any aci-generated text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; gpt-engineer writes files in a user project directory and can execute code with the user’s privileges. If sensitive aci outputs are placed into the coding workspace, gpt-engineer can persist or transmit them via its model/API path. The blast radius includes exfiltration and durable leakage.
conditions: IF aci outputs CRM/email/support data into files or prompts used by gpt-engineer, leakage can occur.
IF the project directory contains sensitive data, gpt-engineer can read and rewrite it.
mitigations: Keep sensitive aci outputs out of the gpt-engineer project directory.
Use a redacted export before handoff.
Restrict the project directory to synthetic or non-sensitive data.
Review generated files for secrets before saving.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate storage and egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci has broad network egress and multiple API integrations, while gpt-engineer has read/write filesystem access and subprocess execution in a per-project scope with shared state via the project directory. Their write surfaces overlap indirectly through files and external services, so concurrent runs can overwrite or desynchronize artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, file races can occur.
IF aci writes artifacts that gpt-engineer also edits, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize edits with a simple handoff checklist.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same files.
Snapshot the directory before each agent run.
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and gpt-engineer can turn text into code and execute generated code with the user’s privileges. If gpt-engineer treats aci output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into committed code or operational actions. The pair therefore has a default path from generated text to downstream action with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses aci output as a source of truth without verification, cascading error is likely.
IF generated code is executed after incorporating aci-produced facts, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require human verification of aci-derived facts before coding.
Separate fact-gathering from code generation prompts.
Disable automatic execution of generated code.
Add a checklist for source validation.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and support data, which may include regulated personal data, while gpt-engineer stores project files locally and can execute code with user privileges. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is moved into the coding workspace or external model calls. I cite both because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from aci is copied into gpt-engineer project files, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF the configured model backend is outside the required jurisdiction, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace.
Use anonymized or synthetic examples.
Confirm retention settings for both tools.
Document the data flow before use.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls.
